tools.name: get_workspace
tools.title: Workspace overview
tools.description:
Workspace name, plan, bot status, owner DM readiness (owner_dm_open,
see add_post_image) and this month's MCP post usage.

tools.name: list_channels
tools.title: Your channels
tools.description:
Channels in this workspace, including ones the bot cannot post to.

Only channels where bot_is_admin is true AND is_active is true can
receive posts — create_post rejects any other channel_id. Check both
fields before calling create_post with a channel from this list.

tools.name: get_channel_stats
tools.title: Channel subscriber stats
tools.description: Subscriber totals and day-by-day joins and leaves for one channel.

tools.name: list_posts
tools.title: Recent posts
tools.description: Recent posts in this workspace, newest first.

tools.name: get_post
tools.title: Post details
tools.description: One post with its text and per-channel delivery status.

tools.name: create_post
tools.title: Create a post
tools.description:
Create a channel post. Text is Telegram HTML; omit scheduled_at to send now.

Every channel_id must have the bot as admin (see list_channels) — one
that doesn't is rejected here, not delivered and left failing silently.

tools.name: publish_post
tools.title: Publish a draft
tools.description: Send a draft now (or at its scheduled time, if it has one).

tools.name: cancel_post
tools.title: Delete a post
tools.description: Delete a draft, scheduled or failed post. Published posts stay.

tools.name: add_post_image
tools.title: Attach an image to a post
tools.description:
Download an image from a URL and attach it to a draft, scheduled or failed post.

⚠️ Side effect the user should know about: Telegram's Bot API has no way
to hand a bot a URL and get back a file_id for it — a bot can only learn
a file_id for something it has itself sent. So this tool downloads the
image, sends it through the workspace bot to the **workspace owner's own
private chat with that bot** to obtain a file_id, then deletes that
message again. The owner will still briefly see (and get a notification
for) a photo arriving from their own bot — mention this to them if they
did not just ask for the image themselves, so it isn't a surprise.

That DM must already be open: the owner needs to have pressed Start with
the workspace's bot at least once, or Telegram refuses the send outright.
This tool checks for that up front and refuses — with a link to the bot
to hand the owner — before downloading anything if it's missing. To find
out ahead of time instead of discovering it from a failed call, check
owner_dm_open on get_workspace.

A post can hold at most 10 media items (Telegram's own cap for a grouped
post); adding an 11th is refused before the download starts.

annotations.title: Attach an image to a post

tools.name: update_post
tools.title: Edit a draft or scheduled post
tools.description:
Edit a draft, scheduled or failed post's text, title or scheduled time.

Only the parameters you pass are changed — omit one (or leave it None)
to keep its current value. scheduled_at follows the same rules as
create_post: ISO 8601 with a UTC offset, a past time is rejected, and an
empty string means "leave unchanged" (there is currently no way to clear
a post's schedule back to "send immediately" through this tool). Once a
post is published, use edit_published_post instead — this tool refuses it.

annotations.title: Edit a draft or scheduled post

tools.name: edit_published_post
tools.title: Edit a published post
tools.description:
Change the text of a post that has already gone out to its channels.

Only for posts that are published or partially published — for drafts
or scheduled posts use update_post instead, which this tool refuses to
touch. Buttons, media and everything else about the post are left as
they are; only the text changes. Telegram is contacted once per channel
the post reached: a failure on one (for example because someone deleted
the message there by hand) does not stop the others — check
edit_results in the response for the per-channel outcome.

tools.name: retry_post_delivery
tools.title: Retry a delivery
tools.description:
Retry delivery for a post's failed or canceled channel target(s).

Pass channel_id to retry just that one channel; omit it to retry every
retryable target on the post at once. This does not talk to Telegram
itself — like create_post, it resets the target to pending so the next
worker pass (within a minute) attempts delivery again; check list_posts
or get_post afterward for the outcome.

tools.name: list_subscribers
tools.title: Channel subscribers
tools.description:
Subscribers of one channel: who they are, when they joined, their
status, and recent activity — newest subscriber first.

Money fields (total spent, lifetime value, payment count, last payment
date, and the count of unlocked paid posts) are left out by default:
they are a person's financial profile, and an agent asked to "tell me
about my subscribers" should not pull that out incidentally — including
indirectly, through sort order (this list is ordered by signup date, not
by payment recency, precisely so the ordering itself does not leak who
has paid). Pass include_spend=True only when the task genuinely calls
for it — e.g. finding top payers.

status filters to one value (see the error for the full list of allowed
values) — omit it to get every status. limit caps the page at 1-100
(default 20).

tools.name: get_subscriber
tools.title: Subscriber profile
tools.description:
One subscriber's card: identity, join date, status, activity.

Same privacy rule as list_subscribers — total spent, lifetime value,
payment count, last payment date, and the count of unlocked paid posts
are omitted unless you pass include_spend=True. Only turn that on when
the task specifically needs this person's financial history, not to
answer a general question about them.
